facts.dates: Apply within 90 days of purchase or install; paid receipt with model number, manufacturer, price and date required

Not for new construction is not stated on this page; product must be new and installed at a PECO electric residence.

facts.claim: $150 at 15.2-17.0 SEER2; $300 at 17.1 SEER2 or higher; both need 11.0 EER2 and 7.8+ HSPF2 as certified by AHRI
facts.eligibility: PECO electric customers; same minimum ratings as ducted
facts.notes: Re-read 2026-10-05 on pecohomerebateprogram.com.

facts.claim: $350 for an ENERGY STAR heat pump water heater; PECO also lists $200 for a natural gas tankless and $50 for a natural gas storage tank water heater for PECO gas customers
facts.dates: Apply within 90 days of purchase or install; paid receipt required
facts.notes: Re-read 2026-10-05 on pecohomerebateprogram.com. Rebate applies where the home receives PECO residential electric (or gas, for gas units) service.

facts.claim: $50 instant rebate at select Home Depot stores and on PECO Marketplace; $25 after install by online application only (PECO Energy Efficiency Portal)
facts.notes: Re-read 2026-10-05. PECO says smart thermostat rebates depend on the heating or cooling system the thermostat connects to, and are for qualified PECO customers. Customers who got an instant discount cannot also claim a rebate.

facts.claim: Air source $225 or $325 (Tier 1 SEER2 15.2+, EER2 11.7+, HSPF2 7.8+; Tier 2 SEER2 16.3+, EER2 12.9+, HSPF2 8.2+); mini-split $225 (SEER2 15.2+, EER2 11.7+, HSPF2 7.8+, rebate based on outdoor unit); ground source $500
facts.eligibility: PPL Electric customers; amount depends on your offer
facts.dates: Equipment installed on or before May 31, 2026 no longer eligible; the deadline is shown when you apply
facts.notes: Re-read 2026-10-05 on each PPL product page. Systems must be ENERGY STAR certified and rated whole-system in the AHRI database (certificates must list the indoor coil and outdoor unit; component ratings do not count). Not available for new construction. The $225 or $325 split is shown as two tiers; we do not state which tier pays which amount beyond the listed ratings.

facts.program: PPL Electric heat pump water heater
facts.notes: Re-read 2026-10-05: ENERGY STAR certified, UEF 3.3 or higher. Equipment installed on or before May 31, 2026 no longer eligible.

Re-read 2026-10-05: ENERGY STAR certified. Home must have an air-source heat pump, fossil fuel heating with central A/C, or an electric furnace with central A/C. Baseboard heat, geothermal and mini-split heat pumps are not eligible. Installs need a labor invoice; self-installed units may be inspected to confirm the heat source.

facts.program: PPL Electric insulation and air sealing
facts.claim: Attic, exterior wall, rim joist and basement wall insulation each up to $200 or $500; air sealing up to $150 ($0.25 per CFM reduction, 10% minimum improvement, $25 minimum rebate)
facts.eligibility: Existing permanent living space conditioned by an electric heat source, or central A/C with non-electric heat; labor invoice required; no new construction, workshops, garages, crawl spaces or outbuildings; new R-value must exceed existing (basement wall: R-15 continuous or R-19 cavity minimum)
facts.dates: Installs on or before May 31, 2026 no longer eligible
facts.notes: Re-read 2026-10-05 on the PPL attic, wall, rim joist, basement wall and air sealing pages. Each insulation page states a rebate of 75% of the project cost based on your existing heating and cooling configuration, up to the listed amount. Air sealing must follow BPI standards with pre and post blower door tests. The higher amounts are for enhanced income-based offers.

facts.claim: Stopped accepting applications in 2013. No active statewide PA solar rebate.
facts.notes: Do not advertise 'up to 35% / $17,500'. Confirm with PA DEP before saying anything about a new state solar program.

facts.claim: Ended for spending after Dec 31, 2025
facts.notes: Applies to solar, battery and heat pump credits.

facts.claim: $500 rebate for an initial residential solar installation; only paid once interconnection is approved and the system is In Service; apply within 90 days of In Service status
facts.dates: No end date stated on the page read 2026-10-05; additions to existing systems are not eligible
facts.notes: Re-read 2026-10-05 on pecohomerebateprogram.com (solar rebate page and its FAQ). Earlier we recorded a closed window (Permission to Operate Sep 2024 to Apr 2026); neither page shows that wording today, so status is active with no stated end. Confirm with PECO (888-573-2672) before relying on it. Needs PVWatts report and interconnection (GPC) printout.

facts.program: PGW EnergySense roof insulation and air sealing
facts.claim: Gas-heated PGW residential customers, retrofits only, BPI-certified contractor, pre and post photos. Finished >=R-49 with air sealing $0.65/sq ft (Affordable $0.95); without $0.60 ($0.90). >=R-38 with air sealing $0.35 ($0.50); without $0.30 ($0.40). Affordable tier: CRP, Hardship Funds or LIHEAP to PGW in last year. Participating contractors can give instant rebates; using one not required. First-come, subject to funds; check processing currently delayed.
facts.eligibility: PGW customers heating with natural gas
facts.notes: Re-read 2026-10-05. Phone 855-749-7658. Program page says rebates run 09/01/2024 to 08/31/2027, first come first served, only for premises on PGW firm natural gas rates.

facts.claim: Free weatherization for households at or below 200% of federal poverty level (priority elderly, disabled, children, high energy users): blower-door air sealing, attic/wall/basement/crawlspace insulation, heating repair or replacement, health and safety. Average spend $8,547 per household.

facts.program: Philadelphia Energy Authority Built to Last
facts.claim: Coordinates home repair, health and energy upgrade programs for underserved Philadelphia homeowners in one process; no dollar amount published. Phone 215-686-4483.
30% credit up to $1,200 a year for improvements placed in service through December 31, 2025. Nothing for 2026 installs.

facts.program: PPL Electric rebate catalog: no battery rebate
facts.claim: PPL Electric's rebate catalog lists 15 items (heat pumps, heat pump water heater, smart thermostat, insulation, air sealing, appliances, A/C). None is for home batteries or energy storage.
facts.notes: PPL catalog re-read 2026-10-05: 15 items, none for batteries or EV chargers. PECO's rebate index (appliance, heating and cooling, new homes, water heating, solar) also lists no battery. Duquesne Light and FirstEnergy PA not readable (see pa-20, pa-27).

facts.claim: ENERGY STAR clothes washer $25, clothes dryer $15, refrigerator $20, dehumidifier $25, air purifier $25 (smoke CADR 51 CFM or more); advanced power strip up to $15; water heater pipe insulation, aerators and showerheads up to $3

facts.claim: Residential solar systems up to 50 kW are eligible for net metering: excess generation is credited at the full retail rate. Renewable Energy Credits are sold through the AEPS system. Interconnection rules differ by utility.
facts.eligibility: Customers of Pennsylvania electric utilities; alternative suppliers may not offer net metering
facts.notes: Read on the DEP residents solar page 2026-10-05. The page also lists Solarize Greater Philadelphia and Solarize Philly as discount programs; it states no dollar amount.

facts.notes: Read the DEP page and pennenergysavers.com 2026-10-05; the site only offers update sign-up. Do not state rebate amounts.

facts.claim: Free weatherization run for the state WAP in the City of Pittsburgh, Allegheny, Washington and Greene counties. Income at or below 200% of poverty. 2025 limits: 1 person $30,300; 2 $42,300; 3 $53,300; 4 $64,300; each extra person $11,000. Need three months in the home and gas and electric bills.
facts.eligibility: Income-eligible owners, or renters with landlord sign-off
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-05. Phone 412-281-2102 for City and Allegheny County.
